# Waste Management Data Collection & Analysis — Pranjal Yadav

> Field project (S.Y.B.Sc. Computer Science, University of Mumbai, 2025–26)
> studying why household waste segregation fails between kitchen and collection
> point across three housing typologies in Mumbai.

## Pages

- [Home](index.html): abstract, key metrics, principal findings.
- [Field Visit](field-visit.html): three observation zones and observation matrix.
- [Methodology](methodology.html): survey design, questionnaire Q1–Q10, processing, ethics.
- [Findings](findings.html): secondary-data analysis, interactive Figures F-1–F-6.
- [Survey](survey.html): primary results N=100, interactive Figures P-S1–P-S5, frequency table.
- [Solutions](solutions.html): conclusions and fourteen recommendations with owners and indicators.
- [Academic](academic.html): certificate, declaration, acknowledgement, guide diary, downloads.
- [References](references.html): 14 cited sources and annexures.

## Data

- [Primary dataset, N=100 (CSV)](data/survey-responses.csv)
- [Full report (DOCX)](data/field-project-report.docx)

## Key figures (exact counts)

- India 2021–22: 1,70,339 TPD generated; 91.8% collected; 53.7% treated.
- Wards: 90.1% claimed vs 48.8% verified segregation (41.3-point gap).
- Survey N=100: 53% single bin; 67% single-chamber vehicles; 87% observed remixing.
